line: A first-person flight over a crayon village to one flower in an old man's garden; then his eyes, and what he says.
line_cn: 第一人称飞过蜡笔画的村子，落在老人花园里的一朵花上；最后换成他的眼睛，和他说的一句话。

camera.expresses: We are someone; what they look at is what matters
camera.serves: a memory; a visit; a stranger arriving

camera.move: Gaze follows a moving person with a lag
camera.serves: longing; shyness; a child watching a parent

camera.move: A low skim over a surface (wheat, water, roofs)
camera.serves: a journey; a return home; a chase
a farewell; a map of a life; an ending

camera.move: Riding something that sways (a flower, a boat, a branch)
camera.expresses: Being small and alive in the wind

camera.move: Hard cut to another person's eyes
camera.expresses: The other side of the same moment
camera.serves: a reveal of who the camera was; a reply

transitions: Transitions are cuts or camera moves;
never a dissolve, never a 3D-looking whip with motion blur.
labels: Words are printed on the page: a handwriting face in the outline colour, written in a character at a time, sitting on blank paper. Never a speech bubble, a box or a plate.

Blank paper is made: leave part of the picture uncoloured (only a strip of sky) and put the words there, clear of what the eye follows. Thin the colour out just before the words arrive; blank paper held empty reads as a mistake.
Bilingual: the Chinese line, then the English line a size smaller underneath, written in after it. Example faces (OFL): Long Cang for Chinese at 110–140 px, Patrick Hand for Latin at 50–64 px.
A wordless film is native; a narrated one prints its lines the same way, at the bottom of the frame, on a paper patch the scene leaves free.
motion: Drawings step at 12 per second; the film is rendered at 24 fps (each drawing held for two frames).
No boil on still things: an object keeps its strokes from drawing to drawing while it doesn't move; it changes only because the camera or the object moves.
Camera paths are smooth splines in time (continuous velocity), starting and ending at rest. Gaze is smoothed as a direction, with a lag, never as a look-at point.
Living things move in a child's way: two key drawings for a repeated action (wings, steps), simple poses, held.

native_moves.name: The camera is someone, never shown
native_moves.does: The viewer learns who from what the world does around them.
native_moves.fits: a pet coming home; a returning soldier's walk through a town; a seed carried by the wind.

native_moves.name: Cut to the other's eyes
native_moves.does: The last shot swaps point of view and shows, small, what the first person was.
native_moves.fits: a parent seeing their child leave; a lighthouse keeper seeing the boat; a teacher seeing a former pupil.

native_moves.name: Passing, not pointing
native_moves.does: Clues are flown past at the speed of the shot, never stopped at.
native_moves.fits: a house's history in its objects; a company's first office; an old route to school.

native_moves.name: Blank paper for words
native_moves.does: Colour only part of the world and print the line where the crayon stops.
native_moves.fits: a dedication; a line of a letter; the name of a place.

native_moves.name: Wind
native_moves.does: Sway, drift and flapping keep held frames alive without a cut.
native_moves.fits: a field at dawn; a waiting room by an open window; a harbour.

score.note: music box, nylon guitar, recorder as the singing voice
